project.name: Buinee — AI Solutions Studio landing page
project.one_liner: Reposition buinee.app from a standalone AI assistant to an AI implementation studio that sets up and customizes tools clients already use (Muse and others) — new landing page identity, structure and copy.

intent.label: Product
intent.value: Public marketing site for an AI implementation/integration studio (buinee.app)

intent.label: Primary user
intent.value: Ghana-based SMB owners and operators evaluating whether to hire Buinee

intent.label: Usage
intent.value: Occasional, evaluation-driven visits before registering a company

intent.label: Primary job
intent.value: Understand the services on offer, see proof it works, and start onboarding

intent.label: Platform
intent.value: Responsive marketing website — redesign of the existing single-page buinee.app landing page, not a new product

decisions.title: Marketing-site redesign, not a new product
decisions.value: This redesigns buinee.app's public landing page (index.html) and its CMS copy schema. The underlying product — registration, dashboard, billing, admin — is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Matches the existing repo (server.py-rendered, CMS-token-driven index.html) and the scope of what the user asked for.

decisions.title: Muse is the flagship service, not the only one
decisions.value: Muse Personal Assistant leads the services list as the flagship integration, alongside WhatsApp Automation, Social Media Management, Business Dashboards, Customer Support Agents, Document & Data Automation, Scheduling & Reminders, and Custom AI Solutions.
decisions.rationale: User corrected mid-session: "Muse is only one of the services we offer, not the only service," after the supplied mockup already showed this exact 8-card structure.

decisions.title: Services grid: the 8 cards from the mockup
decisions.value: Muse Personal Assistant, WhatsApp Automation, Social Media Management, Business Dashboards, Customer Support Agents, Document & Data Automation, Scheduling & Reminders, Custom AI Solutions — each with a one-line description and an arrow link.

decisions.title: 4-step "How it works"
decisions.value: 1. Understand Your Business — 2. Set Up & Integrate — 3. Customize Workflows — 4. You Stay in Control, exactly as laid out in the supplied mockup.

decisions.title: Hero uses the supplied photograph, not an illustration
decisions.value: hero-image1.png (person relaxing, laptop + phone dashboard mockups, WhatsApp/Instagram/Facebook bubbles) is the literal hero asset.
decisions.rationale: User supplied this file specifically alongside the full-page mockup, which places the same image in the hero.

decisions.title: New accent colour: mint/spring green, replacing the current teal
decisions.value: Brand accent sampled directly from the supplied logo/ad: #27F997 (logo mark, "buinee.app" wordmark) and #48EE94 (ad CTA pill) — the same hue family. A deeper, text-safe shade is derived for links/body copy on light backgrounds to meet 4.5:1 contrast; the bright mint is reserved for buttons, badges and icon fills on dark or white surfaces.
decisions.rationale: Pixel-sampled from buinee-logo.png and buinee-ad.png rather than guessed — a supplied visual reference is the source of truth over the current site's teal tokens.

decisions.title: Bold grotesque-sans headline, dropping the current serif hero
decisions.value: Headlines ("Stop spending time formatting and doing reports.") are set in a bold sans, not the current site's serif display face.
decisions.rationale: Directly visible in the supplied mockup and ad creative; treated as source of truth per house style for visual references.

decisions.title: Neutral white/light-grey surfaces, not the current warm cream
decisions.value: Light sections sample as pure white (#FFFFFF) page background with #F8F9FA card surfaces — a neutral palette, replacing the current site's warm cream (#F6F4EF/#EFECE5). Dark sections (hero, footer, testimonial band) sample near-black with a faint green cast (~#000B0F), close to the current dark theme's existing tokens, so the dark side of the palette carries over largely unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Pixel-sampled from the supplied full-page mockup.

decisions.title: Stays a single page with anchor navigation
decisions.value: Home, Services, How It Works and Industries remain anchor-linked sections on one continuous page, matching both the current site's architecture (nav already uses #anchor links) and the mockup's continuous scroll layout.
decisions.rationale: No signal this needs to become a multi-page app; changing architecture would be a much larger, un-asked-for undertaking.

decisions.title: Pricing and Case Studies: anchor or separate page?
decisions.rationale: The mockup's nav lists Pricing and Case Studies as top-level items, but the one continuous page it shows doesn't render dedicated sections for either — Pricing has no visible section and Case Studies isn't drawn at all (only a single testimonial slide).
decisions.question: Pricing already exists as a section on the current site. Case Studies doesn't exist anywhere yet. Should both stay as anchor sections on the one page (fastest, matches today), or become real subpages?

options.label: Both stay anchor sections
options.hint: Fastest — extend the existing Pricing section, add a short Case Studies section on the same page

options.label: Both become separate pages
options.hint: /pricing and /case-studies — more room to grow each, more build effort now

options.label: Pricing stays an anchor, Case Studies becomes its own page
options.hint: Pricing already works as a section; case studies benefit from more room and can be added incrementally

decisions.title: Rights to display Muse's name and logo
decisions.rationale: The mockup reproduces Muse's name and blue swirl mark directly ("Powered by Muse", app screens labelled "Muse"). Using a third party's brand mark without confirmed rights is a real legal exposure regardless of how the business relationship is framed in copy.
decisions.question: Do you have confirmed partner/reseller rights to use Muse's name and logo on the site as shown in the mockup, or should the integration be referenced without reproducing their brand mark?

options.label: Yes, rights confirmed
options.hint: Use Muse's name and logo mark as shown in the mockup

options.label: Name only, no logo
options.hint: Reference "Muse" by name/description; don't reproduce their logo

decisions.title: Existing proven sections carry over beneath the new structure
decisions.value: The integrations logo strip, the detailed invoice-approval workspace demo, and the FAQ accordion from the current page are restyled to the new identity and kept, slotted in below the mockup's Services/How-it-works/Industries sections rather than dropped.
decisions.rationale: The mockup is a reference for the new top-of-page identity and structure, not necessarily an exhaustive spec of every section — dropping working content the mockup simply didn't render that far down would be a silent regression.

decisions.title: Keep the CMS-editable text system
decisions.value: All new headline/body copy is still routed through the existing {{cms:...}} token system, with SITE_CONTENT_SCHEMA in server.py updated to match the new sections, so the admin Site Contents page keeps working for the new copy.
decisions.rationale: Existing infrastructure already solves this; rebuilding the page as static hardcoded copy would silently remove an admin capability that works today.

decisions.title: Primary audience: Ghana-based SMB owners/operators
decisions.value: Retail, restaurants, health/clinics, schools, churches, hotels and professional-services owners — matches the mockup's "Trusted by local businesses" industry strip, GHS-denominated pricing, and the Accra-attributed testimonial.

decisions.title: Occasional, evaluation-driven visits
decisions.value: Visitors browse a handful of times to decide, then register once — not a daily-use surface.
decisions.rationale: Standard for a marketing/conversion site; nothing in the brief suggests otherwise.

decisions.title: Low-stakes interactions on the public site
decisions.value: Nothing on the public page is destructive; no confirmation dialogs needed outside the existing registration/payment flows, which are out of scope for this redesign.
decisions.rationale: Marketing pages carry no real risk beyond a misread CTA.

decisions.title: Full mobile parity
decisions.value: Every new section reflows to a clean single-column mobile layout; nothing is hidden or degraded on phone.
decisions.rationale: The current site is already fully responsive and this is a conversion-focused public page — standard practice, not a judgment call worth blocking on.

decisions.title: WCAG 2.2 AA baseline
decisions.value: Full keyboard operation, visible focus states, 4.5:1 text contrast (driving the deeper green text token in PG-003), labelled controls.

directions.name: Studio Green
directions.tagline: The supplied mockup, built out: mint identity, dark photographic hero, services-first structure.
directions.fit: Directly matches the reference the user supplied — new logo, new accent, new headline system, new services-grid framing. Lowest translation risk between what was approved and what gets shipped.
directions.tradeoffs: Full visual-identity swap (accent, type weight, surface palette) is more work than a copy-only reframe, and the dark-hero-photo + green-badge motif needs to be threaded consistently through sections the mockup didn't fully render (pricing, FAQ).

foundation.Navigation: Top pill nav, anchor links (Home/Services/How It Works/Pricing/Industries)
foundation.Typography: Bold grotesque sans for headlines, current body sans retained
foundation.Primary interaction: Service cards + step-numbered how-it-works + proof/testimonial band
foundation.Icons: Rounded line icons in tinted colour-chip badges, matching the ad creative

directions.name: Minimal Reframe
directions.tagline: Same current visual identity (teal, serif hero), only the copy and section order change to the services framing.
directions.fit: Lowest effort and lowest visual risk — reuses every existing style token, just rewrites headlines/sections to lead with "services we implement" instead of "your AI assistant."
directions.tradeoffs: Doesn't use the new logo, mint accent or the supplied hero photo/ad creative at all — the delivered page would look nothing like what was sent for reference, which is the opposite of what a visual reference is for.

foundation.Typography: Current serif display + sans body, unchanged
foundation.Primary interaction: Same section shapes, reworded and reordered

risks.text: Using Muse's name/logo without confirmed rights is a real legal exposure — blocked on PG-016.
Scope of Pricing/Case Studies (anchor vs subpage, PG-006) changes build effort meaningfully — subpages mean new routes, new CMS schema pages, new SITE_CONTENT_SCHEMA entries.
The bright mint (#27F997) fails text contrast on white and must only be used for large text, buttons or dark-surface contexts — the deeper #0e9f63 carries body text and links.
Threading the new identity through sections the mockup didn't render (pricing cards, FAQ, integrations strip) means some visual decisions will be extrapolated, not directly copied.

assumptions.text: Registration, login, dashboard, admin and billing flows are unchanged — this redesign is scoped to the public landing page and its CMS schema only.
The 8 services listed in the mockup are the current, accurate list of what Buinee offers today.
